title: Patch: hero plates keep one size however many effects they carry
thread:
**Issue #2877 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #2877: Patch: hero plates keep one size however many effects they carry
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

### What it does

The hero plates (`apps/web/src/game/Hero.tsx`, `.hero` in `apps/web/src/game/board.css`) change size whenever a seat gains or loses an effect, and the board jumps with them. It looks janky.

**Why it happens.** `.hero` is one `flex-wrap: wrap` row (`board.css`, the `.hero` rule near line 119) holding the portrait, the seat label, the Jade and Credits gems, the Heroic Power chip(s), the modifier badges (`modifiers-<side>`, R169), the secret badges (`secrets-<side>`, R860) and the Rift badge (`rift-spent-<side>`, R847). Every chip that appears widens the plate; past the seat's width it wraps to a second line and the plate, the seat and the field all grow. On desktop and tablet (`@media (min-width: 761px) and (min-height: 501px)`, `.seat > .hero`) the hero sits in an `auto` grid column between the piles and the mana, so a wider plate also pushes both sideways. Modifier badges are sized to their text (up to `max-width: 18ch`), so a label going "+1" → "+2" moves things too, and R1639000's "Used" mark is put in front of the power chip's name, widening it once the power has been used.

**The principle:** nothing whose count or text changes takes space in the plate's layout.

**The change**

1. **A plate of one size.** Give `.hero` a fixed width and height per layout (custom properties, set in the media queries board.css already has) and drop its `flex-wrap`. The portrait (health, armor, Luck are already badged on it), the seat label and the primary Heroic Power chip live inside it.
2. **A status tray outside the layout.** Move the modifier, secret and Rift badges into one tray hung off the plate, out of flow (`position: absolute` against `.hero`), toward the field (above your hero, below the opponent's) or beside the plate wherever the layout has the room. The builder picks the side per layout; the acceptance below holds the choice to "covers nothing that matters". Keep every testid and data attribute the badges have now (`modifiers-<side>` stays in the DOM even when empty: `modifierChanged` fades it after its last badge goes, BUILD M5-T4).
3. **An allowance per screen size, then "+N".** The tray shows at most this many entries (modifiers in the view's order, then secrets, then the Rift badge), and every chip has a fixed width with an ellipsis:

   | Layout | Media query | Chips shown | Chip width |
   |---|---|---:|---|
   | Desktop | `(min-width: 1025px)` (and not the phone query) | 4 | 18ch |
   | Tablet, portrait or landscape | 761–1024px wide, not the phone query | 3 | 14ch |
   | Phone, portrait or landscape | `PHONE_BAR_QUERY` (`game/config.ts`) | 2 | 12ch |

   When there are more entries than the allowance, the last slot becomes a `+N` chip (N = the entries not shown) that opens the full list in a bubble laid on the page, placed and dismissed the way `ModifierBadge.tsx`'s bubble already is (the same `placement`, closes on an outside press, a resize or a scroll). Each entry in that list still opens its full label the way `ModifierBadge` does (#2321). The three counts are named constants in `apps/web/src/game/config.ts` beside `PHONE_BAR_QUERY` (CLAUDE.md rule 9), with the desktop and tablet queries as constants too; the layout is followed live by a hook in the pattern of `game/phoneBar.ts` (`useSyncExternalStore` over `matchMedia`, a host without `matchMedia` reads desktop). The chip widths stay in board.css.
4. **The smaller width changes.**
   - R1639000's "Used" mark becomes an overlay or corner tag on the power chip (the chip keeps one width used or not), still readable and still first for assistive tech. The `power` testid, `data-used` and the titles are unchanged.
   - The Jade and Credits gems (`hero-jade`, `market-credits-<side>`) take a fixed slot: Credits already shows at 0; Jade at 0 keeps its box with `visibility: hidden` (out of the accessibility tree), or both move onto the portrait as health and armor did. `market-credits-<side>` stays in the DOM at 0 as R1840005 says.

**Out of scope:** extra Heroic Powers beyond the first (R43, `power-<instanceId>`) keep their chips in the plate; they are rare and are drag sources (`game/drag/targets.ts`). A follow-up can fold them. Engine, view and wire are untouched: the client only draws `SideView` (CLAUDE.md rule 7). No card data changes, so no patch fragment and no version.

**Watch:** `board.css`'s note on `.hero button.modifier-badge` (B46: the board must fit a 1024x768 tablet), B29's 44x44 touch floor on `.board .hero` and `.power-button`, B45 (your hero glowing as a target is never under a lifted hand card), and the phone layout's tight seat padding. Read `apps/web/README.md` and the `ui-walkthrough` skill before you start; screenshot a seat with 0, 1 and 8 effects at the six viewports below.

### Acceptance

- A Cypress component spec in `e2e/cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx`, in the pattern of its R504 `describe`, run at each of its six `VIEWPORTS` (1280x720, 844x390, 768x1024, 390x844, 1024x768, 390x664): mount `fullBoardView()` with no modifiers, secrets or Rift on either seat and measure `hero-you`, `hero-opponent` and the field's top; mount it again with 8 modifiers (long labels among them), 2 secrets, the Rift flag, 3 Jade and a used power on both seats; each hero's bounding box and the field's top are within 1px of the first mount.
- The same spec: with the 8 + 2 + 1 entries, each tray shows exactly the layout's allowance of chips (4, 3 or 2, the last of them `+N` with the right N), and with exactly the allowance's number of entries there is no `+N` chip.
- The same spec: no tray overlaps a `zone` element or `hand-you`/`hand-opponent`, and the existing B28 "no horizontal overflow", B29 44x44 and B45 checks still pass at every viewport.
- A vitest in `apps/web/src/game/Hero.test.tsx`: pressing `+N` opens a list holding every entry, each modifier's full label among them; an outside press closes it; `modifiers-<side>` is present with zero modifiers; the counts come from the `config.ts` constants (a mocked `matchMedia` picks each layout, a host without one gets the desktop count).
- A vitest: a used and an unused power chip render the same chip structure (the mark is an overlay, not text before the name), and the "Used" text is still in the chip's accessible name.
- Every existing test in `Hero.test.tsx`, `ModifierBadge.test.tsx`, `secrets.test.tsx`, `animation-targets.test.tsx`, `Board.test.tsx` and the component and e2e specs passes; one changes only where it asserted on an entry that now sits behind `+N`, and says so in the pull request.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test`, `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge apps/web e2e` and `pnpm --dir e2e test:component` are green.

### Blocked by, part of

None.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41562940233)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Hero plates (`.hero` in `apps/web/src/game/board.css`) stop changing size when a seat gains or loses effects: the plate gets a fixed width and height per layout with no wrapping, the modifier/secret/Rift badges move into one out-of-flow tray hung off the plate, the tray shows a per-layout allowance of fixed-width chips with a `+N` overflow bubble, the "Used" mark becomes an overlay on a fixed-width power chip, and the Jade/Credits gems move onto the portrait as overlays. A Cypress spec proves the hero boxes and field top stay within 1px across mounts at all six viewports; vitest proves the tray counts, the bubble, and the Used overlay.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/game/config.ts` | change | Add `HERO_DESKTOP_QUERY`, `HERO_TABLET_QUERY`, `HERO_TRAY_DESKTOP_COUNT` (4), `HERO_TRAY_TABLET_COUNT` (3), `HERO_TRAY_PHONE_COUNT` (2) beside `PHONE_BAR_QUERY` (rule 9) |
| `apps/web/src/game/heroLayout.ts` | new | `useHeroLayout()` (`"desktop" \| "tablet" \| "phone"`, `useSyncExternalStore` over the three queries in the `phoneBar.ts` pattern; no `matchMedia` reads desktop) and `useHeroTrayAllowance()` mapping layout to the counts |
| `apps/web/src/game/Hero.tsx` | change | In-plate set becomes portrait, seat label, primary power, rare extra powers only; Jade/Credits render as `HeroPortrait` children; `UsedMark` keeps its DOM order; badge lists move into `HeroTray` |
| `apps/web/src/game/HeroTray.tsx` | new | Tray (`tray-<side>`), visible entries, `+N` chip (`tray-more-<side>`), overflow bubble (`tray-list-<side>`) reusing `ModifierBadge` and its placement |
| `apps/web/src/game/ModifierBadge.tsx` | change | Export the `placement()` function (and its gutter/gap constants) for the tray bubble; no behavior change |
| `apps/web/src/game/board.css` | change | Fixed `.hero` size vars per layout, `flex-wrap: nowrap`, tray positioning, per-layout chip widths, fixed power width with absolute `.power-used`, portrait gem anchors |
| `apps/web/src/game/Hero.test.tsx` | change | Tray allowance/bubble/empty-presence tests and Used-overlay tests |
| `e2e/cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx` | change | New `#2877` describe: 1px stability, allowance counts, no-overlap |

Must not touch: `crates/*`, `apps/web/src/wire/generated/*`, `spec/*` (no ruling: this is pure client layout, no rules decision, so rule 3 adds nothing; existing R169/R860/R847/R1639000/R1840005 cites stay accurate), `Portrait.tsx`, `contract.ts`, `drag/targets.ts`, e2e support files, `.github/`, `.harness/`, `bot/`.

## Steps

1. Read `apps/web/README.md` and the `ui-walkthrough` skill, then screenshot a seat with 0, 1 and 8 effects at the six viewports as the before-record.
2. In `config.ts`, add `HERO_DESKTOP_QUERY = "(min-width: 1025px)"`, `HERO_TABLET_QUERY = "(min-width: 761px) and (max-width: 1024px)"`, and counts 4/3/2, each with a one-line comment citing #2877.
3. Write `heroLayout.ts`: `useHeroLayout()` subscribes to all three query lists and returns `"phone"` when the phone query matches, `"desktop"` when the desktop query matches, else `"tablet"` (this also covers the 601–760px non-phone gap); server snapshot and no-`matchMedia` host return `"desktop"`. `useHeroTrayAllowance()` maps the layout through the three count constants.
4. In `ModifierBadge.tsx`, export `placement()` unchanged (naming it `bubblePlacement` is fine as long as all callers use the one name).
5. Write `HeroTray.tsx` (`{ side, seat }`, reading `SideView` only): build entries in order — `modifiers` in view order, then `secrets` (`secretBadgeText`), then the Rift flag. Render `<span className="hero-tray" data-testid={tray-<side>} data-count={total}>` holding the always-present `modifiers-<side>` span (same classes, testid, `data-count`, `role="group"`, aria-label), the conditional `secrets-<side>` and `rift-spent-<side>` spans with their current chip markup (extract local `SecretChip`/`RiftChip` used both in the tray and the bubble), and, when `total > allowance`, a `tray-more-<side>` button (`+N`, `data-more`, `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`) where `N = total - (allowance - 1)` and only the first `allowance - 1` entries render as chips. The button opens a `document.body` portal positioned by the shared placement function, dismissed on outside press, resize and scroll exactly like `ModifierBadge`'s effect; the list (`tray-list-<side>`) renders every entry, modifiers as `<ModifierBadge>` (keeps #2321), secrets/Rift as static chips.
6. In `Hero.tsx`: keep portrait, `.hero-seat`, primary `power` button/tag and extra `power-<instanceId>` chips in the plate; move the Jade span (still only when `(seat.jade ?? 0) > 0`) and the Credits span (still only when `marketCredits !== undefined`) into `HeroPortrait` children; replace the three badge blocks with `<HeroTray side={side} seat={seat} />`; keep every testid, `data-*` attribute and title. Keep `UsedMark` as the chip's first child (accessible name still starts with "Used"); its overlay positioning is CSS-only.
7. In `board.css`: set `.hero { width: var(--hero-w); height: var(--hero-h); flex-wrap: nowrap; overflow: visible; }` with `--hero-h: 50px` (48px in the phone query) and a ch-based `--hero-w` per layout (portrait 44px + label allowance + 14ch power + that layout's gaps/padding, plus a small slack term); tune the slack until step 9 passes. Position `.hero-you .hero-tray` above the plate and `.hero-opponent .hero-tray` below it (`top`/`bottom: calc(100% + 2px)`, horizontally centered), single row, compact chips. Fix chip widths with ellipsis: 18ch desktop, 14ch tablet, 12ch phone, `flex: none`. Set `.power-button, .power-tag { width: 14ch; position: relative; }` and `.power-used { position: absolute; top: -8px; right: -4px; }`. Anchor `.hero-portrait .hero-jade` (top-left) and `.hero-portrait .hero-credits` (top-right) at the 22px overlay metrics of the health/armor badges.
8. Extend `Hero.test.tsx`: stub `window.matchMedia` per layout (phone/tablet/desktop, plus a no-`matchMedia` host reading desktop) and assert the visible chip counts equal the imported config constants; pressing `+N` lists all 11 entries with every modifier label, an outside press closes it, `modifiers-<side>` exists with zero modifiers; assert the Used chip keeps `.power-used` first with the same accessible name and that `board.css` pins `.power-used` to `absolute` with a fixed chip width.
9. Extend `board-layout.cy.tsx` with a `#2877` describe in the `R504` pattern at all six `VIEWPORTS`: mount `fullBoardView()` then the same view with 8 long-label modifiers, 2 secrets, the Rift flag, 3 Jade and a used power on both seats, and assert each hero box and the field top within 1px; assert tray chip counts (4/3/2 with `+8`/`+9`/`+10`, none at exactly the allowance); assert the tray rect never intersects a `.zone`, `hand-you` or `hand-opponent` rect. Adjust step 7 values until green.
10. Run the checks in Tests, then re-screenshot the six viewports for the pull request record.

## Tests

- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/Hero.test.tsx` — new `#2877` tray tests (allowance per mocked layout incl. no-`matchMedia`, `+N` list/close/empty-presence) and Used-overlay test.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/ModifierBadge.test.tsx`, `src/game/secrets.test.tsx`, `src/game/animation-targets.test.tsx`, `src/game/Board.test.tsx` — unchanged and green (jsdom reads desktop allowance 4, so the 2+1 fixture badges stay visible; change one only if it asserts an entry now behind `+N`, and say so in the pull request).
- `pnpm --dir e2e exec cypress run --component --spec cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx`, then full `pnpm --dir e2e test:component` before stopping; existing B28/B29/B45 specs must still pass unmodified.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge apps/web e2e`, `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] Plate, field top stable within 1px with 0 vs 8+2+1 effects at all six viewports (Cypress green).
- [ ] Tray shows 4/3/2 chips with correct `+N`, none at exactly the allowance; no tray overlaps a zone or hand.
- [ ] `modifiers-<side>` present when empty; all kept testids/`data-*`/titles intact; extra powers still in-plate drag sources.
- [ ] Used mark is an overlay, first for assistive tech, chip width identical used/unused.
- [ ] All listed unit, typecheck, eslint and component checks green; screenshots retaken.

## Risks

- The phone-portrait seat-to-field channel (~14px) barely fits a chip row; the plan gives the phone tray tighter chip padding, and the Cypress rect test arbitrates — shrink padding before ever touching seat/field geometry (B46).
- Portrait gem taps now route through the portrait press handlers; clicks still bubble to the hero target pick, and a hold opens inspect like the rest of the portrait.
- Tray and bubble briefly duplicate `data-modifier-id`/`data-secret-id` chips while open; all assertions scope inside `modifiers-<side>` / `secrets-<side>` / `tray-list-<side>`, as `secrets.test.tsx` already does.

## Open questions

- None. The one judgment the task leaves (tray side per layout) is settled above: toward the field vertically in every layout, verified by the no-overlap assertions.
```
